title: Personal Loans Credit Policy: Assessing a Second Loan Against the Combined Principal Cap
content:
## Policy

When a borrower who already holds an active Personal Loans loan applies for another, the loans are assessed together. The combined unpaid principal of the borrower's active loans plus the amount financed of the new loan may not exceed the combined principal cap of the new loan's grade; the principal of a loan that the new loan refinances is left out of the sum, and unpaid fees and accrued interest are never part of it. The existing active loan has an amount past due of 0.00. A second concurrent loan (one that does not refinance the existing loan) also requires that the existing loan has at least the second-loan number of consecutive on-time installments, counted under the grade of the existing loan. If the combined amount would exceed the cap, the new loan is approved only for the largest amount that fits under the cap, provided that amount is still at least the grade's minimum loan amount; otherwise the application is declined.

The combined principal cap, the second-loan number of on-time installments and the minimum loan amount are the grade figures of the Personal Loans schedules.

## Terms used

- **Combined principal**: the unpaid principal of the borrower's active loans, less any loan being refinanced, plus the new amount financed.
- **Largest amount that fits**: the combined principal cap less the unpaid principal of the active loans counted.
- **Consecutive on-time installments**: counted backwards from the latest installment due on or before today, the number of most recent installments each paid in full (amounts credited toward it, net of any later-returned payment, reaching the scheduled payment amount) no later than the end of the late-fee grace period, with no late fee charged for it; an installment deferred under a hardship plan is skipped, neither breaking nor extending the run.

## Worked case (hypothetical figures)

A borrower holds one active loan with 28000.00 USD of unpaid principal, nothing past due, and applies for a second Personal Loan Grade D loan of 16000.00 USD, Grade D's cap being 40000 USD. Combined principal is 28000.00 plus 16000.00, or 44000.00, above the cap. The largest amount that fits is 40000.00 less 28000.00, or 12000.00; that is at least Grade D's minimum loan amount of 2000 USD, so the loan can be approved only for 12000.00, and only if the existing loan also shows at least the second-loan number of consecutive on-time installments of its own grade.

## Points of judgement

| Fact on the records | Effect |
|---|---|
| existing active loan has any amount past due | the condition of 0.00 past due is not met |
| new loan refinances the existing loan | the old loan's principal is left out; the second-loan on-time count is not required |
| largest amount that fits is below the grade's minimum loan amount | the application is declined |
